compliance.seismic: Designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 3

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 1828.8 m (6000 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing; short term 5 to 93 percent
environmental.operating-temp: 0 C to 40 C (32 F to 104 F)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C (-40 F to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.timing: 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB connectors and a PTP Ethernet SFP port

performance.packet-buffer: deep buffer from hybrid memory cubes (HMC)
performance.throughput: 12 Tbps and 4 Bpps of forwarding capacity (Q5 ASICs); 192 x 10 GbE, 60 x 40 GbE or 60 x 100 GbE ports (Tables 2 and 8)

physical.mounting: four-post rack kit in the box; spare kits EX4500-4PST-RMK
physical.weight: 41 kg (90.39 lb) with four supplies and three fan modules fitted, AC or DC (Table 30; the rack-mounting topic gives 36.5 kg, 80.5 lb)

platform.asic: Q5 packet forwarding ASICs with hybrid memory cubes

power.psu-ac-input: 100 to 127 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC at 50 to 60 Hz, 11.5 A at 100-120 VAC (Table 21); each supply has one input
power.psu-dc-input: -48 to -60 VDC rated, -40 to -72 VDC operating range, 57.5 A maximum (Table 25); a 40 A breaker is recommended
power.psu-redundancy: four bays, 2N recommended; one supply at 220 VAC or two at 110 VAC run the 60C

thermal.airflow: port-to-FRU (airflow out, front-to-back); three 80 W fan modules at 150 CFM each, and fans in the supplies
thermal.heat-dissipation: 6,825 BTU/hr typical and 8,530 BTU/hr maximum (Tables 21 and 25)

configs.description: The QFX10002-60C as shipped (Table 1 and Table 30): four 1600 W AC supplies and three JNP10002-FAN1 fan modules, all with port-to-FRU airflow.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The DC build QFX10002-60C-DC (Table 1): four 1600 W DC supplies. Mixing AC and DC supplies in one chassis is not supported.
configs.name: dc

configs.description: The spare chassis, JNP10002-60C (Table 3). The guide lists the chassis, the fan module and the supplies as separate spares and does not say what a spare chassis ships with, so it is read as the chassis alone with every bay open (estimated). It takes either feed once supplies are fitted.
configs.name: s

gaps.note: The QFX10002 datasheet address tried (qfx10000-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf under juniper.net/content/dam) returned an HTML 404 page and the product page timed out, so no datasheet is cited and no figure comes from one.
gaps.wanted: the QFX10000 datasheet, for the bundle part numbers

gaps.note: The guide draws the rear only for the 72Q and the 36Q (Figures 4 and 5) and in perspective for the 60C's fan module (Figure 46), so the rear is measured on the studio photograph and every rear position is estimated to about half a millimetre.
gaps.wanted: a flat rear elevation of the QFX10002-60C

gaps.note: The photograph shows a small dark dot above the MGMT legend of the SFP row, and Figure 11 draws a small circle there. Figure 22 numbers 8 callouts and none is it. It is not modelled.
gaps.wanted: the name of that dot (a reset pinhole?)

gaps.note: The guide's four-post procedure names no ear distance in millimetres and draws the rails only in perspective, so no ears position is written, and the spare kit EX4500-4PST-RMK is left out of chassis.kits in this slice.
gaps.wanted: the rail drawing and ear distances, and the four-post kit as a kit contract

gaps.note: The two-hole protective grounding terminal is shown in perspective on a side panel and no flat view places it, so it is not placed. The guide states the screws (10-32 UNF x 0.25 in.) and the lug (Panduit LCD6-14BH-L) but not the hole spacing.
gaps.wanted: a flat side elevation with the terminal, and its hole spacing

gaps.note: The DC supply takes a D-sub 3W3 connector and the library has no 3W3 standard, so the DC supply draws the shell in its skin and offers no seat for the cable plug.
gaps.wanted: a D-sub 3W3 connector in the connector registry

gaps.note: Figure 11 draws small squares in the corners of both jack outlines, and the 72Q's text says "the LED below the port indicates status and link" for its console. The 60C's Figure 22 says nothing of a console lamp and the photograph shows none, so the console is the bare jack.
gaps.wanted: a close-up of the management panel

gaps.note: Table 15 gives one link and activity lamp for the SFP management port and the guide does not say which of the two lamps above the cages belongs to which cage. Each is tied to the cage under it, left to left.
gaps.wanted: the lamp assignment of the two SFP ports

gaps.note: The guide lists in prose what each port takes (QSFP28, QSFP+, DAC, AOC and breakout cables) but no transceiver table, so the port groups declare no interface.
gaps.wanted: the QFX10002 transceiver list from the Hardware Compatibility Tool

gaps.note: The laser-radiation label at the left end of the upper band is drawn as a pale plate. Its words cannot be read at the resolution of Figure 11 or the photograph, so none is drawn.

gaps.wanted: which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp-0-29, qsfp-30-59 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Description and Table 17 - every QFX10002 has port-to-FRU airflow (airflow out, AFO, front-to-back): air enters through the vents of the port panel and leaves through the FRU panel. The guide lists no back-to-front fan module or supply, so the device has no airflow configuration. The module handles are gold in the guide's tables and orange in the photograph (the photograph wins; see the module contracts).

channelization.note: Table 9 - five ports per ASIC (PE0 to PE11, twelve ASICs); within each ASIC the fourth port cannot be channelized and is disabled when one of the other four is, so a fully channelized switch has 192 10 GbE interfaces. It is a configuration of the switch and not a printed mark, and the port groups carry no per-port channel attribute.

colour.note: Median of the bare front face in qfx10002-60c-front-high (#c4c4c8 at the left margin, #bdbcbd near the right). The rear chassis reads #6f7581 at its left strip and #838591 between the supply columns in the rear photograph. The fan faces and the supply handles read #f67b44 and #c76234 in the photograph, the fan bezel median #ec640e.

drawing-vs-photo.note: Figures 11 and 22 and the photograph agree on what is printed: PWR, STS, MAJ, MIN with ALARM down the bracket, MGMT, CON, PTP, PPS and 10M, and the model name. The guide's text (Table 16) names the lamps PWR, STA, MJR and MIN and Figure 22's callout text says STS and MAJ; the silkscreen follows the metal. The figure draws a laser-radiation label as a white box with printed words at the left end of the upper band and a hazard triangle between the bands; the photograph shows the label only as a faint pale outline and the triangle as a thin chevron, neither yellow, so the label is drawn pale, the triangle as an outline, and their words are not drawn. The drawing's group steps are uneven by a millimetre and a half and the photograph's are even, so the mean is used (see ports).

envelope.note: Table 30, Physical Specifications for the QFX10002 (the QFX10002-60C rows): 3.46 in. (8.8 cm) high, 17.36 in. (44.1 cm) wide, 31 in. (78.7 cm) deep "without handles for fans or power supplies". The height is carried as 88.0 mm, the 8.8 cm of the table, 2RU. The face is the body between the folds with no ears drawn. The depth 787.0 mm is the 78.7 cm of the table. WEIGHT CONFLICT - Table 30 gives the 60C 90.39 lb (41 kg) with FRUs installed, AC or DC, and the rack-mounting topic gives 80.5 lb (36.5 kg); the table is carried, as it is the guide's specification table.

fan-module.note: Table 3 and the install topic - the 60C takes JNP10002-FAN1 ("a different fan module that has a different orientation"), modelled as qfx10002-jnp10002-fan1. The 72Q's QFX10002-FAN-S fan is not seated here.

gate-1.note: Both flat sources pass. Figure 11 (g050765, 1505 x 591 px, embedded image extracted from the PDF) gives a frame 1472 px wide (outline centres x 14.5 to 1486.5) and 293.5 px tall (y 150.0 to 443.5), aspect 5.015 against the stated 441.0 / 88.0 = 5.011, 0.1 percent out. Scaled on the width it is 3.338 px per mm across and 3.335 down. The front photograph's face is 1887 px wide (x 100 to 1987), 4.279 px per mm, and 373 px tall, aspect 5.06, 1 percent out; the rear photograph's panel is 1886 px wide (x 99 to 1985), 4.277 px per mm. Positions are taken per axis on those scales and read to about half a millimetre; each is estimated, as it is read off a picture and not off a dimension.

grounding.note: Connect the QFX10002 to Ground - a two-hole protective grounding terminal on the chassis, for two 10-32 UNF x 0.25 in. screws and a Panduit LCD6-14BH-L lug. The figure is a perspective view, and no flat figure places it, so it is not modelled. See the gap grounding-terminal.

held-sources.note: The intake folder for the Juniper exqfx documents (COVERAGE.md, SOURCES.md and INVENTORY.md and its photographs) is not present on the host that built this device, so the check for a held photograph, Visio stencil or 3D model could not be made. Only the public sources named above were used. If a held model exists it may refine the estimated positions.

hundred-gig-marks.note: The 72Q and 36Q mark their 100 GbE ports with a fine line under the socket. The 60C has no such line in Figure 11 or in the photograph, because all 60 ports take QSFP28 at 100 GbE (Table 2).

lifecycle.note: No end-of-life dates are carried: Juniper's own end-of-life pages were not read for the 60C, and the aggregator dates the 72Q's slice carries were not checked for this model.

logo.note: The maker's logo at the top right is not drawn. It is reserved as the region logo-zone, 25.2 x 7.0 mm, read off Figure 11 (the logo spans 413.7 to 438.1 across and 1.7 to 7.8 down). The model name below it is plain text, 415.5 to 437.2 across and ending at 12.2 down, and is drawn.

mgmt-panel.note: Figure 22 (g051219) callouts 1 to 8 and Figure 11, measured on Figure 11 per axis. This is a different panel from the 72Q's: callout 1 is the USB port, upright, centred at 395.7, 53.0 with the USB symbol above it; callout 2 the four status lamps, PWR over STS at 403.0 across and 52.6 and 57.5 down and MAJ over MIN at 408.2 inside a bracket, with the word ALARM down its right side; callout 3 the em0 RJ-45 (1000BASE-T) management port (MGMT) and callout 4 the RJ-45 console (CON) stacked in one shield outline at 420.2 across, 45.9 and 59.1 down in the figure's outline; callout 8 the em1 SFP management port (MGMT) at 391.2 across and 69.0 down; callout 7 the PTP Ethernet SFP port (the guide calls it ETH, the panel prints PTP) right of it at 405.45; callout 6 the PPS SMB at 424.7, 73.0 and callout 5 the 10 MHz SMB at 432.8, 73.0. Two small round lamps above the two SFP cages at 402.7 and 408.4 across and 65.8 down are the SFP port lamps (Table 15 - one link and activity lamp). The two RJ-45 jacks are placed at the registry's 13.2 mm height one under the other from 38.6 to 65.0 mm, 2 mm taller as a pair than the drawn shield (24.6 mm), so that the PTP and CON legends clear the console jack. Jack sizes come from the registry; the drawing's housing outlines are not used for size. The printed bracket round MAJ and MIN is not drawn (a line round two lamps would paint over them), and the word ALARM is drawn as five stacked letters.

mounting.note: Mounting a QFX10002 in a Rack and Table 45 - a four-post kit ships in the box (rear mounting blades, front mounting brackets, 4x6 mm flathead screws) and spare kits are ordered as EX4500-4PST-RMK. The rack must have its rails 28 to 31 in. (71.1 to 78.7 cm) apart front to back. The guide gives no ear distance in millimetres and no rail drawing that can be measured and says the chassis must be supported at all four corners, so no ear position and no kit is written, as for the 72Q. EX4500-4PST-RMK is not listed under chassis.kits. See the gap rack-mounting.

port-leds.note: Figure 17 and Table 13 - each QSFP port has one bicolour LED, "triangle shaped". The strip between the two cages of a column draws an up triangle at its left, four small slots and a down triangle at its right, in Figure 11 and in the photograph. The up triangle is the upper port's lamp and the down triangle the lower port's, as the triangles point at their ports. The lamp centres are 1.4 mm and 17.0 mm right of the cell's left edge, 12.4 mm below the upper cage's top. The slots are drawn as one dark plate per column. Table 13 gives the states: green steady is a link (all four sub-channels up when channelized), green blinking is activity, slow green is the beacon, amber steady is some but not all sub-channels up and amber blinking is activity on some sub-channels.

port-numbering.note: Figure 11 and the photograph print 0, 6, 12, 18 and 24 above the upper row of the upper band and 1, 7, 13, 19 and 25 below it, and 30, 36, 42, 48 and 54 above the lower band's upper row and 31, 37, 43, 49 and 55 below it: the first number of each group, as the 72Q's drawing does and as the 36Q photograph prints fewer. Each column holds the even port above the odd one and the ports run left to right, the upper band holding 0 to 29 and the lower band 30 to 59 (Table 9 lists the physical ports 0 to 59). Numbering starts at 0. Interface names are not printed on the metal and the guide's Table 9 gives physical port numbers only, so none is carried.

ports.note: Figure 11 and Tables 2 and 8, counted - 60 QSFP28 cages in four rows of 15 columns: two bands, each two rows of 15 columns in five groups of three, each group one six-port cage, with a gutter between groups carrying a field of hexagonal vent holes. The columns step 19.3 mm in the drawing (cell lefts 70, 134 and 199 px on the lower band of the figure) and in the photograph (19.5 mm), which is 1.6 percent wider than the 19.0 mm of the QSFP ganged registry entry the 72Q sits on; the figure's pitch is used, on the cell the registry gives (18.5 mm). The group step is 78.45 mm (the figure's five groups read 78.3 to 79.1 mm apart, the drawing being a little uneven, and the photograph 79.2 mm; the mean is used, with both bands alike as the photograph shows them), which leaves a 20.55 mm gutter. The first column's left edge is at 16.6 mm. The upper band's rows are at 11.4 and 27.7 mm and the lower band's at 52.5 and 68.8 mm (row step 16.3 mm, which leaves the lamp strip between a cage's bottom edge and the next cage's top). Counts confirmed by Table 2 and Table 8.

power-supplies.note: Tables 4 and 5, Table 30 and the redundancy text - the 60C has four bays, ships with four 1600 W supplies, and unlike the 72Q and the 36Q its bays are NUMBERED VERTICALLY from the top left to the bottom right "which matches CLI output": 0 over 1 in the left column and 2 over 3 in the right. At 220 VAC one supply runs the switch and at 110 VAC two are needed. The guide recommends twice what is needed (2N), with feed A on supplies 0 or 1 and feed B on 2 or 3, and the remaining slots covered with a power supply cover. Mixing AC and DC supplies is not supported. The supplies are the family's JPSU-1600W-AC-AFO and JPSU-1600W-DC-AFO, modelled by the 72Q's slice and reused as they are; Table 3's CLI output lists only an AC supply for the 60C ("AC AFO 1600W PSU for QFX10002-60C") and none for the DC build, which Table 24 supplies with the same DC product number (estimated).

rear.note: Measured on qfx10002-60c-rear-high (the guide has no flat rear figure of the 60C), per axis from the rear left edge (the chassis right side as seen from the front) at 4.277 px per mm. Power supply bays are 74.1 x 40.6 mm in two columns at x 9.2 and 91.2 and two rows at y 2.5 and 43.9 (the photograph's supplies are 73.4 x 39.7 mm; the library's supply is 74.1 x 40.6). Fan module faces are 81.0 x 82.0 mm at x 172.0, 260.9 and 349.8 and y 3.2, on an 88.9 mm pitch. The ESD socket is centred at 435.9, 23.0 with the ESD symbol below it. Fan numbers 0, 1 and 2 with a fan icon and a lamp are printed at 168.5, 257.4 and 346.3 across, the lamp at y 77.7. Power symbols with the digits 0 and 1 are printed at x 86.8 between the supply columns and 2 and 3 at x 168.0 between the right column and the first fan, at y 8.7 and 48.8. Two small round fixings sit between the supply columns at y 20.7 and 71.2. A vertical legend at the left edge reads "AC INPUT:100-240V ~ 60-50Hz 12.5A" and "DC INPUT:-48V TO-60V = 40A (FOR EACH POWER SUPPLY)".

rear-legend.note: The legend prints 12.5A for AC; the guide's Table 21 gives 11.5 A at 100-120 VAC for the 60C and 12.9 A for the 72Q (printed 14A on the 72Q's Figure 4). The DC line prints 40A; Table 25 gives 57.5 A maximum for the 60C. The photograph of the real unit wins for what is printed; the guide's table is carried in the power attributes.

reset-button.note: The 72Q's Figure 21 numbers a reset button; the 60C's Figure 22 lists none. The photograph shows a small dark dot above the MGMT legend of the SFP row (about 388.5, 64.5) that no figure or table names. It may be a reset pinhole, and is not modelled; see the gap unnamed-dot.

spare-chassis.note: Table 3 lists the chassis spares as QFX10002-72Q-CHAS-S, JNP10002-60C and QFX10002-36Q-CHAS-S, beside CLI outputs QFX10002-72Q, QFX10002-60C and QFX10002-36Q. The 60C's spare is therefore the part number JNP10002-60C and not a "-CHAS-S" name. The guide does not say what a spare chassis ships with, so it is read as the chassis alone with every bay open (estimated).

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) turns the lower cage of a belly to belly pair by 180 degrees. It is not applied here, because qfx10002-60c-front-high shows both cages of a column the same way up (the silver latch strip high in each opening, the dark module body below it) and Figure 11 draws both rows alike. The lamp strip lies between the rows.

usb-and-slots.note: The guide names no USB revision (Figure 22 callout 1, "USB port"), and the photograph shows a silver body with a black tongue, which is neither colour the library's skins carry, so the white USB 2.0 skin is used and no 3.0 is claimed. The four small slots between the two lamps of each column are drawn as one dark plate 9.4 x 2.8 mm (the drawing shows two rows of four).

vents.note: Figure 11 - a hexagonal punching above the upper band, between the two bands, below the lower band, a column of hexagons in the gutter between groups, a strip at the left of each band, and fields beside the logo, beside the management jacks and below the SFP cages. They are drawn as repeating patterns inside simplified outlines and not hole for hole. The two rows between the bands are drawn below the printed numbers 1 to 55, which sit on the hexagon field in the metal.
